'''Inba no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''inba no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''inba kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled the central part of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
*According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ōjin|lt_ja=応神朝}}, '''{{ill|Itsukori-no-Mikoto|ja|伊都許利命}}''', the eighth-generation descendant of {{ill|Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto|ja|神八井耳命}}, was appointed kuni no miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Hasetsukabe clan|ja|丈部氏}}''' (''hasetsukabe-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}).

== Base ==
=== Territory ===
The kuni no miyatsuko's territory was the region then known as '''Inba Province''', corresponding to the later '''{{ill|Inba District|ja|印旛郡}}''' of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} — present-day {{ill|Narita, Chiba|ja|成田市|lt=Narita City}}, {{ill|Sakura, Chiba|ja|佐倉市|lt=Sakura City}}, {{ill|Yachimata, Chiba|ja|八街市|lt=Yachimata City}}, {{ill|Yotsukaidō, Chiba|ja|四街道市|lt=Yotsukaidō City}}, {{ill|Inzai, Chiba|ja|印西市|lt=Inzai City}}, and {{ill|Inba District|ja|印旛郡}} in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}.

== Tutelary deity ==
*{{ill|Makata Shrine|ja|麻賀多神社}}
*:A shrine in {{ill|Narita, Chiba|ja|成田市|lt=Narita City}}, Chiba Prefecture, enshrining {{ill|Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto|ja|稚産霊命}}. Among the auxiliary shrines on its precincts is Inba Kokuzō Shrine.

=== Tombs ===

== People ==
[[File:印波國造伊都許利命墓.jpg|thumb|250px|Tomb of Itsukori-no-Mikoto]]

*'''{{ill|Itsukori-no-Mikoto|ja|伊都許利命}}''' (''itsukori no mikoto'')
*:A {{ill|Kofun-period|ja|古墳時代}} figure, kuni no miyatsuko during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ōjin|lt_ja=応神朝}}.

== Descendants ==
*{{ill|Hasetsukabe-no-Ōmaro (Shimōsa Province)|ja|丈部大麻呂 (下総国)|lt=Hasetsukabe-no-Atai Ōmaro}}
*:On the 16th day of the second month of {{ill|Tenpyō-shōhō|ja|天平勝宝}} 7 ([[755]]), while being dispatched to {{ill|Tsukushi|ja|筑紫}} as a {{ill|sakimori|ja|防人|lt=frontier guardsman}}, he composed a verse preserved as poem 4389 of volume 20 of the ''{{ill|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集}}''.

{{quotation|''shio-bune no  hesako so shiranami  niwashiku mo  ouse-tamau ka  omoaenaku ni''

(Like the white waves that cross the bow of a tide-borne boat — was I called up so suddenly, when I had not thought I would be?)<ref>''Man'yōshū'' (vol. 6), "Complete Translation of the Japanese Classics 7," p. 267, Shōgakukan, 1987.</ref>}}

*Hasetsukabe-no-Atai Ushikai
*:A {{ill|Nara-period|ja|奈良時代}} {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} and Inba District {{ill|chief|ja|大領}}. The ''{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}'', {{ill|Ten'ō (Japanese era)|ja|天応 (日本)|lt=Ten'ō}} year 1, first-month entry records that he was granted Outer Junior Fifth Rank Lower for contributing military provisions for the Emishi pacification campaign.
